title: Elimination of indeterminacy
statement:
Let $T$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq T$ be quasi-compact open, and let $W\to T$
be separated and of finite type, with $W_U\to U$ an isomorphism. There is a
$U$-admissible blow-up $T'\to T$ ([sk-def-nagata-admissible]) whose strict
transform $W'\to T'$ is an open immersion. The modification can first be
chosen so that $U$ is schematically dense in $T'$.

This is Stacks 081S. Its main ingredient is flattening by blow-up
(Stacks 081R): if $W\to T$ is of finite type and quasi-separated and is flat
and locally of finite presentation over $U$, then its strict transform under
a suitable $U$-admissible blow-up is flat and of finite presentation. After
[sk-lem-nagata-boundary-divisor], this strict transform contains the inverse
image of $U$ schematically densely and is the identity there, so it is an
open immersion. Conrad's account of Deligne's proof (Conrad, *Deligne's notes
on Nagata compactifications*, Theorem 2.4) reaches the same conclusions
through partial sections ([sk-thm-nagata-sketch-conrad]).

external.place: Conrad's account of Deligne's proof (Conrad, *Deligne's notes on Nagata compactifications*, Theorem 2.4) reaches the same conclusions through partial sections ([sk-thm-nagata-sketch-conrad]).

proof.text:
First blow up a finite-type ideal supported exactly on $X\setminus U$
so that $U$ becomes scheme-theoretically dense. Apply
[sk-thm-nagata-sketch-conrad] with $V=U$ to the section
$U\to Z$. Refine once more by a product with an ideal cutting out
$X\setminus U$. The strict transform is now exactly the
scheme-theoretic closure of the original section. The extended section
has closed graph $\Gamma_{f'}\simeq W$ containing $U$ schematically
densely, so this closure is $\Gamma_{f'}$. Hence $Z'\simeq W$ is open
in $X'$. This is the Deligne–Conrad route in the diagram; the
flattening route also recorded in the detailed chapter is not needed here.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $T$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq T$ be quasi-compact open, and let $W\to T$
be separated and of finite type, with $W_U\to U$ an isomorphism. There is a
$U$-admissible blow-up $T'\to T$ ([sk-def-nagata-admissible]) whose strict
transform $W'\to T'$ is an open immersion.

This is Stacks 081S, proved here without flattening by blow-up. A first
$U$-admissible blow-up makes $U$ schematically dense
([sk-lem-nagata-boundary-divisor]). The inverse of $W_U\to U$ is a section
of $W\to T$ over $U$; by Conrad's account of Deligne's proof (Conrad,
*Deligne's notes on Nagata compactifications*, Theorem 2.4), which rests on
Zariski's Main Theorem, it extends after a further admissible blow-up to an
open containing the preimage of $U$, with closed graph
([thm-nagata-conrad-elimination]). The composite blow-up is $U$-admissible
([sk-lem-nagata-sketch-blowups]), and the closed graph, containing the graph
over $U$ schematically densely, is the strict transform. So the strict
transform is isomorphic to an open of $T'$.

proof.text:
First blow up a finite-type ideal supported exactly on $T\setminus U$, so
that $U$ becomes scheme-theoretically dense
([sk-lem-nagata-boundary-divisor]). Apply [thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] with
$V=U$ to the section $U\to W$ inverse to $W_U\to U$. Refine once more by a
product with an ideal cutting out $T\setminus U$, and compose the blow-ups
into one $U$-admissible blow-up $T'\to T$ ([sk-lem-nagata-sketch-blowups]).
The extended section is defined on an open $W_0\subseteq T'$ and has closed
graph $\Gamma\simeq W_0$ in $W\times_TT'$, containing the graph over $U$
schematically densely. The strict transform $W'$ is the scheme-theoretic
closure of that graph, so $W'=\Gamma\simeq W_0$, and $W'\to T'$ is an open
immersion.
